answer: Anchor every agent identity to a trellis of mutual attestations rooted in a verified kernel of established peers: each new identity must earn signed endorsements from several independent, long-lived agents who stake reputation on it. A farm can whisper cheap claims into the void, but it cannot fabricate the years of cross-checked history its endorsers hold — each extra identity costs one more genuine relationship plus a bond that burns if the identity misbehaves, so the marginal cost of the hundredth fake dwarfs the first.
